---
title: "Two models from the field"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_highs  <- requireNamespace("highs", quietly = TRUE)
has_glpsol <- !is.null(tryCatch(multimod::get_multimod_glpsol(), error = function(e) NULL)) &&
  file.exists(multimod::get_multimod_glpsol())
has_julia  <- nzchar(Sys.which(multimod::get_multimod_julia()))
has_python <- isTRUE(tryCatch(multimod::mm_check_python(packages = c("pyomo", "highspy"))$ok,
                              error = function(e) FALSE))
osemosys_dir <- Sys.getenv("MULTIMOD_OSEMOSYS_DIR", unset = "")
has_osemosys <- nzchar(osemosys_dir) &&
  file.exists(file.path(osemosys_dir, "src", "osemosys.txt"))
```

```{r setup}
library(multimod)
```

The toy model of the other articles fits on one screen. This article runs
two published models written independently of multimod: OSeMOSYS, which is
read from its public source, and the energyRt reference model, which ships
with multimod. Both are energy system models; neither was written with
multimod in mind. Chunks that need a solver or the OSeMOSYS files run only
where those are present; the numbers quoted in the text are from a run with
everything installed.

## OSeMOSYS

[OSeMOSYS](http://www.osemosys.org/), the Open Source Energy Modelling
System, is written in GNU MathProg. Its repository
[OSeMOSYS/OSeMOSYS_GNU_MathProg](https://github.com/OSeMOSYS/OSeMOSYS_GNU_MathProg)
(Apache License 2.0, copyright 2010-2015 OSeMOSYS Forum steering committee)
holds the model file `src/osemosys.txt` and the UTOPIA test case
`tests/utopia.txt`. Nothing of it is bundled with multimod; this section
reads a local clone whose path is in the environment variable
`MULTIMOD_OSEMOSYS_DIR`. The reference result for UTOPIA is the objective
glpsol reports on those two files, 29446.86.

The reference for OSeMOSYS is Howells, M., Rogner, H., Strachan, N., Heaps, C., Huntington, H.,
Kypreos, S., Hughes, A., Silveira, S., DeCarolis, J., Bazilian, M. and
Roehrl, A. (2011). OSeMOSYS: The Open Source Energy Modeling System. An
introduction to its ethos, structure and development. *Energy Policy*,
39(10), 5850-5870. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enpol.2011.06.033>

```{r osemosys-read, eval = has_osemosys}
ose <- read_gmpl(file.path(osemosys_dir, "src", "osemosys.txt"),
                 file.path(osemosys_dir, "tests", "utopia.txt"))
ose
```

The reader returns 11 sets, 61 parameters, 68 variables and 95 equations.
Twenty-six parameters carry UTOPIA data; six are formulas over other
parameters (discount factors, the capital recovery factor, the annuity),
and the rest take their declared defaults, among them a *parametric*
default, `DiscountRateIdv` defaulting to `DiscountRate[r]`.

```{r osemosys-structure, eval = has_osemosys}
validate(ose, stop_on_error = FALSE)$valid
as_gams(ose$parameters$CapitalRecoveryFactor$formula$expr)
cat(as_latex(ose$equations$CAa1_TotalNewCapacity$rhs))
```

### JuMP

Formula parameters become Julia dictionaries computed from the data at run
time, and the parametric default becomes a nested `get()`:

```{julia, eval = FALSE}
# Each variable is declared over a full set product
@variable(model, RateOfDemand[REGION, TIMESLICE, FUEL, YEAR] >= 0)
@variable(model, Demand[REGION, TIMESLICE, FUEL, YEAR] >= 0)
@variable(model, StorageLevelYearStart[REGION, STORAGE, YEAR] >= 0)

@objective(model, Min, sum(TotalDiscountedCost[r, y] for r in REGION, y in YEAR))

optimize!(model)
println("Termination status: ", termination_status(model))
println("Objective value: ", objective_value(model))
```


```{r osemosys-jump-write, eval = has_osemosys}
ws <- tempfile("osemosys-")
dir.create(ws)
write_jump(ose, model_dir = ws)
data_jl <- readLines(file.path(ws, "solvers", "jump", "data.jl"))
cat(substr(grep("^CapitalRecoveryFactor = Dict", data_jl, value = TRUE), 1, 160), "...\n")
```


```{r osemosys-jump-solve, eval = has_osemosys && has_julia}
j <- solve_jump(ose, ws, verbose = FALSE)
j$objective
j$status
```

The objective matches glpsol's 29446.86.

### Solved in R, from the matrix

The same model goes through the matrix route without any generated code.
OSeMOSYS declares every symbol over a set product with no domain mapping,
restricts 34 of its 95 equations with data-dependent conditions, references
lagged years (`y-1`, `y+1`) and defines six parameters by formula; the matrix
route expands the declared sets, evaluates the conditions, resolves the
lags and computes the formulas itself.

```{r osemosys-highs, eval = has_osemosys && requireNamespace("highs", quietly = TRUE)}
h <- solve_highs(ose, attach = FALSE)
h$objective
nrow(build_row_index(ose))   # glpsol generates exactly this many rows
```

### Known limitations

Four storage-bracket equations (`SC2_*`, `SC4_*`) assemble with no
coefficients on this case; UTOPIA's storage is inactive, so the objective is
unaffected, and `model_to_lp()` reports them in a warning.
`write_gams()` output of this model is readable but not yet runnable without
edits. There is no Pyomo reader.

```{r osemosys-cleanup, include = FALSE}
if (exists("ws")) unlink(ws, recursive = TRUE)
```

## energyRt

[energyRt](https://github.com/optimal2050/energyRt) is an R package for
energy system models that writes its own GAMS, MathProg, JuMP and Pyomo
code. `example_models$energyRt` holds one of its reference scenarios, the
"TOPIA" kit (seven regions, seasonal timeslices, a base horizon), parsed by
`read_gams()` from the GAMS template energyRt generates and populated with
the scenario's data.

```{r energyrt-provenance}
str(example_models$energyRt$metadata)
```

The dataset is derived from energyRt, Apache License 2.0, copyright the
energyRt development team. The GAMS source is kept beside the parsed model:

```{r energyrt-source}
gms <- example_models$energyRt$gams$model
length(gms)
i <- grep("^eqTechCap", gms)[1]
cat(gms[i:(i + 4)], sep = "\n")
m <- example_models$energyRt$multimod
m
```

### The matrix route

```{r energyrt-lp, eval = has_highs}
lp <- model_to_lp(m)
dim(lp$A)
r <- solve_highs(m, attach = FALSE)
r$objective
```

The model has about nineteen thousand rows and columns.

### The code-generation routes

The same model goes through each generated language; the objective is the
one to compare.

```{r energyrt-ws}
ws <- tempfile("energyrt-")
dir.create(ws)
```

```{r energyrt-gmpl, eval = has_glpsol}
write_gmpl(m, model_dir = ws)
g <- solve_gmpl(m, ws, verbose = FALSE)
c(objective = g$objective, status = g$status)
```

```{r energyrt-jump, eval = has_julia}
write_jump(m, model_dir = ws)
j <- solve_jump(m, ws, verbose = FALSE)
c(objective = j$objective, status = j$status)
```

The generated Julia, one constraint:

```{r energyrt-jump-code, eval = has_julia, results = "asis"}
jl <- readLines(file.path(ws, "solvers", "jump", "model.jl"))
i <- grep("@constraint", jl, fixed = TRUE)[1]
cat("```julia", jl[i:(i + 4)], "```", sep = "\n")
```

```{r energyrt-pyomo, eval = has_python}
write_pyomo(m, model_dir = ws, export_vars = TRUE)
p <- solve_pyomo(m, ws, solver = "highs", verbose = FALSE, load_results = TRUE)
c(objective = p$objective, status = p$status$termination)
```

With everything installed the four routes return 46398.42.

The GAMS source this model came from can also be regenerated:

```{r energyrt-gams}
out <- write_gams(m)
length(out)
```

Any energyRt scenario enters the same way:
`energyRt::multimod_from_energyRt()` builds the model from an interpolated scenario,
with the structure from the GAMS template and the data from the scenario's
tables.

```{r energyrt-cleanup, include = FALSE}
unlink(ws, recursive = TRUE)
```
